Forensics: the cursor seat is a STATEMENT-COUNT question (flow.c:2081, depth-3 weighting) - three pre-RA src++ statements give src refs 26 and the target's $a3/$a2 seat in ordinary C (new chassis q1,

rederive: m2c confirms f1 IS the target's emitted shape, and the ORIGINAL cc1psx seats f1's cursors the same way ours does - the 3-session 'same refs, different seat' contradiction is the C, not the t

frontier.hypothesis: Door (b) is still open if reorg can copy a shared advance_src block's insn into one of the two CONDITIONAL branches that currently carry NOP delay slots (bne $s1,$v0 at 8003DF38, bnez $v0 at 8003DF48) - the target proves the copy path fires in this function, just on the loop-back branch.
frontier.mechanism: reorg.c:3057-3061 admits non-jump insns and CONDITIONAL jumps into the steal-from-branch-target path at reorg.c:3169 (add_to_delay_list (copy_rtx (next_trial)) + reorg_redirect_jump), which is a genuine instruction created after flow.c fixed reg_n_refs. s8's class kill covers UNCONDITIONAL jumps only (reorg.c:3059). q1 already carries the target seat at src refs 26 and is exactly one addiu $a3 short.
frontier.next_probe: On the q1 chassis, dump with BB2_DBR_DEBUG=1 via tmp/grind/func_8003DE14/s8/dump.sh and read which candidate insns reorg considered and rejected for the two NOP-slot conditional branches; then spell forms in which the zero test's fall-through runs into an unconditional jump whose target is the shared src++ block, so next_trial is the addiu $a3 itself. Gate on build_insns == 173 first, then read the $a3/$a2 disposition.

frontier.hypothesis: The four-door accounting assumes the target's pre-RA stream equals its emitted stream minus the single reorg comparand copy; a pre-RA stream of 175 whose cross-jump deletes a [sh dst],[addiu dst] pair would give dst 35 weighted refs (pri 30172 > src 27118) and land on 173.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c:2020 find_cross_jump requires >= 2 matching insns and do_cross_jump deletes them from the redirected arm; if the matched pair is a dst store plus a dst increment, dst pre-RA = 5 sh x3 + 3 addiu x6 + 2 = 35 while src stays 32, flipping the allocation order without touching src at all. This session's objection is that the redirected arm would then emit as a bare j, which the target does not contain - but that was reasoned from tail alignment, not measured against do_cross_jump's actual redirect placement.
frontier.next_probe: Read do_cross_jump (jump.c) for where the new label is planted and whether the redirected arm keeps its own store; then spell an f1 variant with five *dst = stores and three dst++ where two arms store the SAME pseudo and jump to the same label, and measure build_insns plus the ALLOCDBG refs for dst.

frontier.hypothesis: s7 swept the cursor model ONE input at a time; a JOINT (refs, live_length) move is unsearched and the combined thresholds are much closer than either alone - e.g. src refs 29 (one shared pixel lhu) with src live 65 puts pri(src) at 17846 against dst's 17931.
frontier.mechanism: pri = floor_log2(refs) * refs / live * 10000, so dropping src across the floor_log2(32)=5 -> floor_log2(29)=4 step costs only 3 weighted refs instead of 6, and the residual gap can then be closed by a 6-insn live-length extension instead of the 31 a pure live move needs. tools/ra_solver/inverse.py has only ever been run with single-atom bounds on this pair.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run inverse.py global on the f1 model with depth 2 restricted to the cursor pair and joint atoms (refs_down 108 combined with live_extend 108 / live_shrink 109), then check whether any joint vector has a C spelling that preserves the target's two lhu and four addiu $a3.
